meta.title: Urdu Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 49 expressions · 33 everyday, 10 idioms, 6 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 49 Urdu set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 33 everyday phrases, 10 idioms and 6 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Urdu → English (see the Urdu, recall the meaning) and English → Urdu (see an English meaning, recall the Urdu) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the level decks, Urdu A1 to B2, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the four, so they can be studied together without repeating an entry. IT IS SMALL, AND THAT IS THE SOURCE'S SIZE: these are every Urdu expression English Wiktionary defines that passes the deck's filters, and Wiktionary's Urdu is a fraction of its Hindi. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases and does not mark as idiomatic — mostly greetings and everyday formulas used as one piece. The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words', and the PROVERBS the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs. Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Urdu sentences contain them, an expression that is a verb being counted in any form of that verb; Tatoeba's Urdu is small, so only 6 of the 49 are found there at all, and the rest follow in the order of how common their rarest word is. Every expression is printed in the Urdu script, right to left, with Wiktionary's romanisation beneath it. Real example sentences come with 6 of the 49 expressions, three apiece for 0, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword (whether it speaks depends on an Urdu voice being installed on your device). Sources. Expressions, meanings, romanisation and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, then a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0) and the wordfreq project's Urdu list (CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR.
